relations.note: All four Aratta-cycle poems explicitly call Enmerkar the son of Utu.
Utu is invoked as a joyful witness to Enmerkar’s triumph.
Enmerkar repeatedly addresses his divine patron Inana as his sister.
Enmerkar claims Inana’s bed and companionship; she shares a throne-dais with him.
Inana endorses Enmerkar’s demands and instructs him to send a messenger.
relations.source: Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta

relations.note: Inana sends Enmerkar a ritual strategy through his messenger Lugalbanda.
Enki grants Enmerkar wisdom to answer Aratta’s impossible demand.
relations.source: Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta

relations.note: Enki clears reeds and drains Uruk’s marshes for Enmerkar.
Enmerkar sends an incantation describing Enki changing human speech.
relations.source: Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta

relations.note: Nisaba opens her house of wisdom for Enmerkar during the contest.
relations.source: Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta

relations.note: Enmerkar claims Enlil granted him the true crown and scepter.
Enmerkar is described as a ruler who takes Enlil’s counsel.
Enmerkar claims Aruru extended both breasts and nursed him.
Enmerkar claims Ninurta held him upon his lap, validating his kingship.
Iškur sends Aratta a storm and grain, frustrating Enmerkar’s economic pressure.
relations.source: Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta

relations.note: Inana’s spousal link to Enmerkar is juxtaposed with her love for Dumuzid.
relations.source: Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta

relations.note: Lugalbanda serves as Enmerkar’s subordinate warrior and elite commander.
Lugalbanda volunteers as Enmerkar’s messenger and carries his complaint to Inana.
A damaged chronicle apparently makes Adapa curse Enmerkar for an unidentified offense.
Fragmentary texts place Enmerkar and Adapa near a tomb with a broken metal door.
Learned tradition assigns Nungalpiriggal to Enmerkar as his heavenly descended sage.
The Seleucid king-and-sage list pairs Enmerkar with the sage Nungalpiriggal.
relations.source: Uruk List of Kings and Sages

relations.note: If Seuechoros is Enmerkar, Aelian’s story makes him Gilgamos’s grandfather.
Some modern Assyriologists identify Aelian’s distorted Babylonian king-name with Enmerkar.
David Rohl identifies Enmerkar with Nimrod using disputed analogies and etymology.
